title: Expectations, (in)stability and (in)viability in realistic overlapping cohorts models
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
summary_en: Standard overlapping-generations (OLG) models with naive expectations can produce unrealistic dynamics when calibrated to plausible demographic and saving parameters. Molnár and Simonovits work through several realistic OLG specifications and characterise when adaptive (naive) expectations produce stable, viable saving paths versus when they generate instability or non-viable consumption profiles. The paper helps clarify why some OLG calibrations used in pension and tax-policy work need careful expectation-formation specifications to deliver credible welfare comparisons.
data_used: Theoretical OLG model. Calibration parameters drawn from standard demographic and savings data for European economies.
policy_relevance: Pension-system simulation models used by Hungary's MNB, Pénzügyminisztérium and ÁKK rest on OLG foundations. The paper highlights that expectation-formation assumptions can flip the qualitative results of welfare comparisons across pension reforms — a methodological caution for any agency running dynamic pension simulations.
